capacity_definition.safe_capacity_formula: C_safe(n) is the largest profile-equivalent active-interaction load that passes every workload SLO, keeps the declared production headroom, and includes the required failure reserve at topology size n.
capacity_definition.hard_capacity_formula: C_hard(n) is the largest profile-equivalent load that still passes functional SLOs before production headroom is reserved; it is reported for optimization and cannot be admitted in production.

optimization_exit_rules: A component cannot exit density optimization while a repeatable dominant bottleneck has an untested source-level remedy with a credible five-percent-or-greater safe-capacity gain.
A higher hard capacity does not count when safe capacity, correctness, quality, isolation, drain, recovery, or failure reserve regresses.

If two consecutive source-level experiments each improve safe capacity by less than three percent and profiling shows no new dominant software bottleneck, record the measured frontier and move to the next component.
Hardware-specific acceleration requires a separate cost and operations ADR; standard Linux networking remains the baseline.

scaling_curves.homogeneous_unit: one node of an unchanged role-specific hardware and configuration class
notes: Each component role is measured separately before a mixed Cell curve is accepted.
A passing endpoint total cannot hide a component pool whose added nodes contribute less than the marginal floor.

scaling_curves.homogeneous_unit: one calibrated Cell with the same role mix, profile slice, hardware classes, and failure reserve
notes: Cell placement and durable data shards must prevent a growing global coordination tax.
If the curve bends, the shared bottleneck is sharded or removed before more servers are added.

scaling_curves.homogeneous_unit: one additional Cell-equivalent durable write, event, presence, directory, and object-ingest load slice
notes: PostgreSQL, Redis, NATS, object storage, owner directory, and event fanout are measured as shared services rather than hidden inside Cell totals.
A shared service that fails this curve must partition, shard, batch, cache, or leave the synchronous hot path.

x-ivekit-invariants: Every scaling curve starts at point one with aggregate linearity one.
Every aggregate-linearity point exists in node_or_unit_points and appears exactly once.
node_or_unit_points and aggregate-linearity points are strictly increasing.
C_safe is computed with the same workload profile, hardware class, configuration class, and failure reserve at every point.
A 100,000-interaction endpoint run fails the architecture gate when any required single-node density or marginal-efficiency gate fails.
Production deployment scales from measured demand and safe capacity; it does not reserve 100,000 interactions when actual demand is lower.
